newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bank BOS debut Monday seen at high premium.
newsitem.headline: Polish bank BOS debut Monday seen at high premium.

text.p: Poland's Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA (BOS) should start trade at a significant premium to its 29-zloty issue price on the Warsaw bourse's main market on Monday, possibly around 40 zlotys, analysts said.
In November investors subscribed for 13,071,226 shares in the bank's initial public offering of 1.2 million shares at 29 zlotys each.

"Those who bought the bank on the primary market didn't gain from the bourse's January bull run and are going to want to make some money, so I don't think they'll sell below 40 zlotys," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
Other analysts, who would not give a debut prediction, saw an impressive start for the stock nonetheless.

"Perhaps one concern is the liquidity -- if we have a lot of people rushing in then obviously they're going to pop the price...and we could have some weakening afterwards," said Matthew Czepliewicz, an analyst at Salomon Brothers in London.
Otherwise analysts said a debut of around 40 zlotys could lead to BOS extending gains next week.
Analysts said BOS would be boosted by its core activity of financing environmental projects, which other Polish banks should prove eager to join.
They said the debut price could be kept down by the central bank's decision on Monday to raise obligatory reserves on zloty call and currency deposits, which hurt listed banks this week.
Otherwise analysts said BOS looked good, with Czepliewicz giving it a price-earnings ratio of five for 1996 and about 4.6 for 1997.
"They have good municipal connections for a bank of their size and they have a clean balance sheet, so they're starting off life on the right foot," Czepliewicz said.
